subject: Medsuite trial orchestration & compliance checklist
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@medsuite.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Medsuite trial orchestration & compliance checklist

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan for the PoC and can evaluate the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Recap from call:
- Primary constraints: PHI handling, audit logging, and SOC2 evidence requirements.
- Traffic profile: bursty inference from production UI (peaks 300r/s for short windows), mostly short prompts, some longer context for chart summarization.
- Desired timelines: 4–6 week technical PoC, procurement/contracting parallel.

Proposed PoC approach (recommended path)
- Week 0–1: Kickoff and security intake. We run a short Dedicated trial (reserved test pool) so you can validate throughput and latency without exposing data on shared-hosted tenants.
- Week 2–3: Integration and workload runs with prefix/KV caching enabled, automated evals against your prompt set.
- Week 4: Review success criteria and discuss migration to Private VPC if audit/legal requires full network separation.

Success criteria draft (please confirm/adjust):
- Functional: API integration end-to-end, model outputs comparable to baseline (no >10% regression on key prompts).
- Perf: p95 latency < 120ms for 16-token completion baseline under your typical burst profile.
- Reliability: no more than 1% error rate on inference calls across test window.
- Security/compliance: required logs (audit, access) available and retention policy validated.

Stakeholder asks: please confirm the technical and procurement contacts so we can pull them into the kickoff calendar. From our side: Dev will lead the setup, Marcus will own SRE/benchmarking, and I’ll coordinate procurement and the SOW.

Attachments: Medsuite_PoC_Primer.pdf (short SOW + checklist)

Proposed immediate next step: 30-min kickoff this week to confirm stakeholders and sign off on SOW draft. I’m available Wed/Thu morning PST.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

--
Note: If you prefer starting with Hosted for a very fast smoke test we can, but given PHI and audit items we recommended Dedicated as the lowest friction path to validate performance while keeping data isolation control.

From: Samira Khan <samira@medsuite.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh@medsuite.ai>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@medsuite.ai>, procurement@medsuite.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Medsuite trial orchestration & compliance checklist

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 3:22 PM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Hi Samira —
> 
> Thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan for the PoC and can evaluate the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Thanks Kimberly — this is great context and aligns with internal notes from our security review. A few clarifications from our side:  

1) Deployment preference: Our security and compliance team strongly prefers Private VPC/on-prem for any production PHI workload. That said, we are open to a short Dedicated PoC to validate perf and integration while the VPC procurement work runs in parallel.

2) Success criteria tweak: The latency target is reasonable — please add a throughput check at 95th percentile burst handling (we measure bursts as 200–350r/s over 30s). For quality, we’ll provide representative prompt sets (clinical summarization + extraction) — expected fidelity must remain within our internal tolerances (we’ll share thresholds).

3) Timeline & stakeholders: We want to move quickly. Proposed contacts: Rajesh Iyer (CTO), Elena Morales (Head of Security), and our procurement alias (procurement@medsuite.ai). Legal will also need to see a draft SOW.

I’ve attached our security intake: HITRUST-Checklist.xlsx — it lists required evidence and logging expectations. We can do kickoff Wed 10–10:30am PST if that works.

Thanks,
Samira
VP Product & Ops | Medsuite AI
samira@medsuite.ai

Attachments: HITRUST-Checklist.xlsx

Thanks for the quick response and the HITRUST checklist, Samira — that’s super helpful.

Updated plan based on your guidance:
- Kickoff: Wed 10:00–10:30am PST to confirm stakeholders and sign off SOW draft (I’ll send calendar invite).
- PoC scope: 4-week Dedicated trial focused on: integration, perf under burst profile, and logging/audit verification. We’ll run the full prompt set you provide in weeks 2–3.
- Parallel work: Redwood legal/ops will start the Private VPC intake so we can estimate lead time for VPC migration if required.

Owners (internal):
- Dev Patel: PoC engineering lead (setup, test harness, credentials)
- Marcus Lin: SRE & benchmarks (throughput/latency verification)
- Kimberly Park: Commercial & SOW coordination

Draft success criteria (finalize on kickoff):
- p95 latency < 120ms for baseline interact flows
- Burst handling: maintain p95 < 200ms under 300r/s 30s window (we’ll run runs to validate)
- Quality: model output hit rate within thresholds you provide
- Security: audit log delivery to your collection endpoint + evidence for access control & key management

I’ve attached a draft SOW for review: PoC_SOW_draft.docx. I’ll also drop the HubSpot deal link in the invite so procurement/legal can reference the same record.

If everyone is good with kickoff time I’ll send the invite and attach the SOW + PoC checklist.

Best,

Kimberly
